text:
Samir: noticing a p95 jump in CPH pop since ~08:12 UTC, p95 went from ~85ms -> ~620ms, throughput down ~18%. Any ideas?
Ava: saw the alert too, linking grafana panels: https://grafana/redwood/d/CphPop - looks like packet reordering + retry amplification around the same window.
Samir: copying the top-line from traces: most affected route -> upstream peer AS12345, a lot of out-of-order acks and retransmits.
Lukas: running mtr from an affected host now, output attached:
```
HOST: cph-pop-01
Loss%  Snt   Last   Avg  Best  Wrst StDev
  0.0%    10   1.2ms  1.8   1.0   9.5   2.5
 12.0%    10  22.0ms 45.6  21.6 110.0 36.9  <-- mid-path peer
```
Priya: runtime logs show kernel selector flipping from fast-vector-kern to safe-fallback at ~08:13 for many sessions. Kernel switch adds ~120-200ms tail per request while it warms. Also KV cache coldstart events spike.
Samir: can you paste the kernel-selection log snippet?
Priya: 
```
[08:12:58] selector: probe rms=0.12 latency_ms=78 choose=fast-vector-kern
[08:13:01] selector: probe rms=0.46 latency_ms=210 choose=safe-fallback
[08:13:07] selector: fallback reason=packet_reorder_detected
[08:13:25] kvcache: expire-trigger keyspace=low hit_rate=0.63 -> 0.42
```
Ava: interesting — the selector is marking reorders as risk and switching kernels which disable some batching optimizations (to be safer), that explains both p95 and throughput drop. Why are we seeing reorder?
Lukas: peer reported internal maintenance + BGP flap around that time, partial queues causing reorder. They're acknowledging noisy behavior.
Samir: mitigation options: 1) pin kernel to fast-vector temporarily for all CPH POP traffic, 2) force batch-heuristic to aggressive low-latency mode (reduce batch size/timeout), 3) steer traffic to alternate peer/POP. Which is least risk?
Priya: pinning kernel is low-risk short-term but will risk correctness if reorder causes duplicates. Forcing low-latency batching reduces queueing and will limit warm-up cost on kernel switch. Steering to alt peer is safest but depends on capacity.
Ava: can we run a controlled change: set batch_timeout_ms=6 (from 12) for CPH route and increase kvcache grace window to avoid mass evictions, then monitor 10m?
Samir: yes please. Priya, can you push config via runtime feature flag? format: `envoy-route/cph/batch_timeout_ms=6,kvcache/grace_ms=60000`
Priya: pushing now -> `deploy-bot` starting rollout to cph pop (canary fraction=10%).
deploy-bot: rollout started: envoy-route/cph@canary=10% (by Priya)
Priya: can confirm 10% canary healthy for 2m, p95 down ~40% on canary hosts. Scaling canary to 50% now.
Lukas: peer reports BGP partial resolved ~08:30 UTC and packet reorder rate falling.
Samir: once canary is good, increase to 100% and then remove kernel pin fallback rule.
Priya: increased to 100% at 08:36, monitoring...
monitoring-bot: cph-pop p95: 620ms -> 180ms in 20m after changes. throughput recovering to -4% delta.
Ava: nice. We should still follow up with peer for postmortem and consider adding a less-sensitive reorder threshold in kernel selector to avoid flipping kernels on short bursts.
Samir: Agreed. Action items: Lukas to get contact/PMR with carrier + network timeline, Priya to open runtime change to tune selector hysteresis + kvcache grace for flapping peers, Ava to file post-incident eval for batching heuristics vs reorder.
Priya: created ticket RM-4491: "selector: increase reorder hysteresis for kernel flip; add metrics to track kernel-change churn". Linking: https://redwood/ops/RM-4491
Lukas: opening ticket NET-782: "CPH peer AS12345 BGP flap / packet reorder investigation" and pinging carrier NOC.
Samir: thanks all. If anything else pops, reply here. Marking incident as mitigated for now — will wait for carrier postmortem before closing. :white_check_mark:
Ava: tiny note for postmortem: include a mini-experiment to replicate reorder + kernel switch locally so we can test fallback strategies without customer impact.
Priya: will add to RM-4491 as a subtask.
Samir: closing the thread in ~24h unless new signals show up.
